measurement_scope: Real end-to-end pipeline throughput (Zeek -i lo live capture -> Kafka -> stream_consumer.py -> detectors -> alerts.json), NOT an isolated Python-loop micro-benchmark (see scripts/benchmark_throughput.py for that). Single self-contained 12-core mobile laptop (i7-1255U) running the capture, broker, and detector pipeline on the same cores as this load generator -- not dedicated hardware, not a real NIC (loopback only). Numbers here reflect single-laptop self-contained capacity, not a production appliance. Measured with a real Kafka broker running (docker compose kafka+zeek services) and stream_consumer.py's micro-batched detector dispatch (ODIN throughput plan Phase A1 -- see docs/benchmark_results.json's 'batching_speedup_x'). A prior run on the pre-batching code, same generator config, peaked at 22.2 events/sec avg 21.47 -- this run's peak_events_per_sec/avg_events_per_sec below is the batched-code result on the same hardware and load shape.

alert_latency.note: This bundles Zeek's own flow-close/log-flush delay with real pipeline transit time (Kafka + consumer dispatch + detector compute) -- it is NOT a pure pipeline-overhead number, especially for long-lived flows.

hardware: 12 logical cores (see docs/benchmark_results.json for the exact CPU model)
run_to_run_variance_note: This single run's numbers should NOT be read as a precise measurement -- three back-to-back runs immediately before this one, same generator config, on this same machine, produced peak/avg events/sec of (291.9/147.02), (142.6/80.32), and (83.2/79.01): a declining trend, not noise around a stable mean. Root cause: this machine was concurrently running 10 Docker containers sharing 12 cores -- this repo's own kafka+zeek services PLUS a pre-existing, independently-running 8-container multi-host attack-lab (recon/c2/ddos/exfil scenario generators) started in an earlier session -- so available CPU for stream_consumer.py's detector dispatch was shrinking across runs as that lab's own background traffic accumulated, not because the batching fix (Phase A1) regressed. scripts/benchmark_throughput.py's isolated, no-Kafka measurement is the controlled, repeatable evidence for the batching speedup itself (a clean 4.74x, verified twice); this E2E number's honest takeaway is narrower: the live Zeek->Kafka->batched-consumer pipeline is demonstrably functional and, even under heavy shared-machine contention, sustained 79-292 events/sec against a ~297 events/sec offered load -- a real, if noisy, multi-fold improvement over the pre-batching E2E baseline of peak 22.2 / avg 21.47 events/sec measured under lighter background load.
